preconditions.description: The number of suspects is between 1 and 100,000.
The number of suspects who told the truth is between 0 and n.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= ai <= n for ai in answers)
preconditions.description: Each suspect's answer refers to a valid suspect number.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n lines.

postconditions.expression: all(output[i] in ['Truth', 'Lie', 'Not defined'] for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: Each line in the output is either 'Truth', 'Lie', or 'Not defined'.

postconditions.expression: any(all(truths[i] == (answers[i][0] == '+' and i + 1 == int(answers[i][1:]) or answers[i][0] == '-' and i + 1 != int(answers[i][1:])) for i in range(n)) for truths in itertools.combinations([True, False], n) if sum(truths) == m)
postconditions.description: There exists a combination of m true statements such that each suspect's answer matches their truthfulness.
